summary: Multipath proxy fanout causing tenant quota attribution anomalies during large CDN-backed uploads
description: Issue summary: Customer StreamlineLabs reports repeated 429 throttles during large multipart uploads served through their CDN+edge proxy. The tenant's token bucket appears to be drained at 1.8–2.2x the expected rate compared to identical uploads executed from a non-CDN path. Impact: Intermittent production errors for ingestion pipeline, failed uploads, and elevated support noise. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod (us-east) behind a CDN layer that uses an upstream connection pool and health-checks.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Upload a set of 256 multipart embedding files concurrently through the customer's CDN origin (same bucket+API key).
2) Observe ingestion progress over the customer's dashboard and our rate-limiter metrics.
3) Repeat the same upload from a single-hosted test VM without CDN intermediary.
4) Compare token consumption per completed file between the two runs.
logs:
Example excerpts (rate-limiter logs):
2026-03-10T14:03:12Z tenant=streamlinelabs api_key=sk-prod-*** conn_id=upstream-42 tokens_consumed=128 reason=ingest
2026-03-10T14:03:12Z tenant=streamlinelabs api_key=sk-prod-*** conn_id=upstream-43 tokens_consumed=126 reason=ingest
2026-03-10T14:03:12Z tenant=streamlinelabs api_key=sk-prod-*** conn_id=upstream-42 tokens_consumed=127 reason=ingest
Observation: multiple distinct conn_id values appear for the same logical client workload; bucket decrement rate aligns with sum across conn_ids, not deduped by api_key+upload-id.
investigation:
Hypothesis 1: CDN / upstream proxy connection pooling + keepalive behavior is causing the gateway to attribute the same logical client to multiple connection identifiers, which the rate-limiter treats as separate actors, doubling/tripling accounting.
Hypothesis 2: Health-checks and prefetch workers are opening short-lived upstream connections that perform preflight / partial uploads and are being counted against the tenant.
What we checked: rate-limiter accounting logic, token-bucket keying (currently keys on api_key + connection_id), proxy access logs from customer (timestamps show multiple upstream connections spawned per single client-side connection), and Grafana heatmaps (spike aligns with CDN edge refresh window ~every 30s).
Partial findings: Replaying the upload through a test origin that preserves client IP and uses connection reuse results in correct token accounting. Replaying via CDN with default config reproduces *~2x* token consumption.
Next steps: request CDN config that preserves client IP or use X-Forwarded-For; patch rate-limiter to prefer api_key+upload-id dedupe for multipart ingest as a temporary change; coordinate with infra to add a short-lived mitigation to map upstream connection IDs to api_key when they are from a known trusted proxy pool.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Malik (Support): Customer first reported this at 13:50 UTC. They see 429s starting ~5 minutes into large parallel ingest jobs. Provided upload ids and sample request IDs: req_9a2f, req_9a30.
2026-03-10 — Evan Brooks (SRE): Assigned and began gathering rate-limiter traces. Noted duplicate conn_id patterns. Requested CDN edge config and any proxy pool IP ranges from customer.

2026-03-10 — StreamlineLabs (Customer): Sent proxy mapping and confirmed they use FastEdge CDN which does aggressive multipath origin connections and occasionally rewrites SNI. Provided origin-config: keepalive=on, pool_size=8.

2026-03-11 — Evan Brooks (SRE): Ran controlled test comparing origin-direct vs CDN: direct=expected token rate, via-CDN=1.9x tokens. Attached Grafana dash link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/streamlinelabs?orgId=1
Prelim workaround suggested: throttle the CDN pool size or enable client_ip preservation.

2026-03-11 — Dev on call (Ingress): Noted rate-limiter currently keys on api_key+conn_id to prevent websocket hijack accounting; changing that requires a risk review. Created infra ticket gh:infra/replace-proxy-metrics#4123 to track safe dedupe implementation.
2026-03-12 — Aisha Malik (Support): Customer accepted temporary mitigation to increase tenant burst credit while we coordinate CDN config changes. They requested ETA for permanent fix.
2026-03-12 — Evan Brooks (SRE): ETA for mitigation rollouts: temporary policy change + burst increase today; engineering patch for keying logic estimated 5 business days pending review.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied 2026-03-12: increased burst allowance for StreamlineLabs and added a traffic-class exception for their tenant to suppress immediate 429s while we implement a safe dedupe path. Follow-up actions: (1) work with infra to implement api_key+upload_id dedupe for multipart ingest accounting (tracked in gh:infra/replace-proxy-metrics#4123); (2) ask customer to enable client IP preservation or reduce origin pool_size to 1–2 to avoid multipath fanout; (3) add a monitoring alert for token-rate-per-upload > 1.5x baseline. Will update when PR merged and canaries complete.
notes: Risk considerations: switching keying logic may open a path for misattribution if an attacker can reuse upload_id; change gated behind review and additional validation on upload_id freshness and signature.
